description: Online used-car marketplace for Mexico, buying, reconditioning, and reselling cars with a 7-day return policy to solve the trust gap in informal used-car markets. At Series A: a capital-intensive inventory model attacking a $25B TAM dominated by individual sellers and dealer lots.
current_status: Recovered from 75% down round ($8.7B → $2.2B, March 2025). Raised $300M Series F from a16z in Feb 2026, a16z's largest single LatAm investment. First month of global profitability December 2025. 120K transactions in 2025 (+40% YoY). Fintech arm originating $600M annualized in loans. AI agents handling majority of customer interactions.

founder.name: Carlos García Ottati
founder.background: Colombian-Mexican serial entrepreneur. Previously founded Linio (LATAM marketplace e-commerce, acquired by Falabella) — deep understanding of LATAM distribution and informal consumer markets.
founder.problem_fit: HIGH on distribution and LATAM retail dynamics; MEDIUM on the capital-intensive reconditioning operations side, which is closer to Carvana than to Linio.
founder.execution_evidence: Shipped Linio through a full LATAM footprint and exit. Rebuilt Kavak twice — once through COVID-era growth, again through the 2025 restructuring and comeback.
founder.red_flags: Linio's unit economics were famously aggressive. Pattern repeated at Kavak (capex + country expansion burning margin) before the 2025 reset.

stage_context.vs_base: Kavak's trust-gap thesis and $25B TAM suggested upside vs Series A base rate (+13pp thriving, +2pp breakout). Capex risk of inventory + reconditioning was under-weighted at the time — the realistic downside landed closer to zombie than dead.

verdict: Kavak survives IF (a) December 2025 profitability extends to full-year positive EBITDA, not just one month, (b) fintech loss ratios hold as auto lending scales from $600M to $1B+ through a Brazilian and Mexican credit cycle, (c) valuation recovery justifies the $2.9B total raised without requiring another down round. Most fragile: (b) — scaling auto lending at 100% growth in emerging markets with untested credit models through a rate cycle has broken larger companies.
top_risk: Inventory financing cost + rapid country expansion burning gross margin; a single inventory cycle downturn erases 18 months of equity
top_opportunity: Attached financing (Kuna) monetizes buyers a second time and is structurally higher-margin than the car transaction itself
actual_outcome: The top_risk hit exactly as modeled. Expansion to Colombia, Peru, Argentina, Turkey, Brazil stretched balance sheet. Peak $8.7B valuation collapsed 75% to $2.2B by 2025. Painful restructuring — exits, layoffs, country shutdowns — but the core Mexico unit became profitable by late 2025. Kavak survived the storm; still unclear if the exit multiple justifies the $2B+ invested across all rounds.
